newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Two ships held up in Portugal in ITF protest.
newsitem.headline: Two ships held up in Portugal in ITF protest.

text.p: Two ships were subjected to delays in Lisbon port on the fourth day of a week-long European campaign by the International Transport Workers' Federation (ITF) against flags of convenience, a union spokesman said.
"Two ships are stuck in Lisbon right now," Mario Falgueiro, spokesman of the Federation of Dockers' Unions, said.

The ITF was staging a week of industrial action across Europe against flag of convenience (FOC) ships from May 12 to 16. Ships in four countries including Portugal had been subject to boycotts and delays, the ITF has said.
The term flag of convenience refers to ships flying the flag which is not the national flag of the country of the owner.
The ITF has long said FOC registers tend to have more substandard ships and poorer wages than national registers.
Falgueiro told Reuters that inspections of Liberian- and Maltese-registered ships by port workers in Lisbon had revealed that their crews had no contracts and were paid very low wages.

"The captain of the Liberian-registered Loretta D, a general cargo vessel, prevented a second inspection of the ship," Falgueiro said. "Operations (by dockers) on the ship were interrupted at 1830 local (1730 GMT) on Wednesday."

He said that an inspection of the Maltese-registered Eurolady, transporting fertilisers, had shown that its crew had no contract, but he expected that an agreement with the ITF to regularise their wages would be signed shortly.

Earlier this week, the 29,400 dwt Panamanian-registered bulk carrier Sharpnes was briefly held up in the port of Leixoes in northern Portugal while an ITF agreement was negotiated for its Russian crew.

The owner of Sharpnes agreed to sign a wages deal with the ITF covering its whole fleet of 47 ships and to pay wage arrears, the Federation of Dockers' Unions said in a statement. --David Brough, Lisbon newsroom +351-1-3538254
